stories.title: Operation Clean Sweep launches an India programme with AIPMA
stories.summary: Operation Clean Sweep, the resin stewardship programme, has launched OCS India with AIPMA, PlasticsToday reports. The move takes the programme's international footprint to 18 countries and strengthens its presence across Asia. India's plastics makers now have one more sweep to sign up for.

stories.title: Huhtamaki India's profit falls 19% as raw material costs jump
stories.summary: Huhtamaki India's net profit fell 19.3 per cent year on year to ₹297 million in the third quarter, even as net sales grew 23.7 per cent to ₹7,481 million on volume growth and price pass-throughs. Raw material costs rose 33 per cent and EBITDA margin slipped to 7.77 per cent.

stories.title: Emmbi Industries' profit dips as sales rise
stories.summary: Emmbi Industries' consolidated net profit fell 12.2 per cent year on year to ₹25.14 million in the September quarter, while standalone net sales rose 11.3 per cent to ₹1,359.89 million. The polymer products maker also booked a flood related inventory loss at Silvassa and has filed an insurance claim.

stories.title: BHU clears 400 kg of plastic waste in a campus drive
stories.summary: Banaras Hindu University collected 400 kg of plastic waste for disposal during a campus cleanliness drive under Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters 6.0, The Times of India reports. The rainwater harvesting pond at its garbage dump yard was cleaned too. Pending matters, it turns out, include plastic.

stories.title: A 17 year old's campaign kept 8.1 million plastic utensils out of landfill
stories.summary: Landon Hoberman, 17, from New Jersey, campaigned for restaurants to stop automatically adding plastic cutlery to takeaway and delivery orders. The effort is credited with stopping 8.1 million single use utensils going to landfill and saving restaurants more than $200,000. Asking first turned out to be the cheaper option.

stories.title: A Quebec home is built from panels holding about 200,000 bottles of plastic
stories.summary: A 1,078 sq ft two bedroom home in Saint-Rémi-d'Amherst, Quebec, was built with structural panels made from the equivalent of about 200,000 recycled plastic bottles, and the shell went up on site in three days. The PakVert system comes from PakVille, founded by engineer Parinaz Pakniat.

stories.title: Welsh researchers make a biodegradable plastic from seaweed
stories.summary: Researchers at Aberystwyth University's IBERS institute have combined alginate, a seaweed extract, with other biological compounds to make a biodegradable plastic that is stronger and more flexible, Canadian Plastics reports. They say it could one day replace fossil fuel based plastic films in food packaging.

stories.title: New York Post warns about microplastics in an everyday drink
stories.summary: Researchers say a drink more than half the US population has daily is often loaded with microplastics, the New York Post reports. Experts suggest avoiding plastic cooking utensils and plastic containers for reheating, and new research says tea drinkers should avoid brands using plastic tea bags.

stories.title: SoapMate flip top closure promises one handed dish soap
stories.summary: MRP Solutions' SoapMate is a flip top closure that brings one handed, mess free dispensing to dish soap, hand soap and personal care products, Packaging World reports. It is aimed at the moment when the other hand is holding a dripping plate.

stories.title: TH Group cuts 600 tonnes of plastic a year with packaging changes
stories.summary: TH Group, owner of the TH true MILK brand, has cut plastic use by about 600 tonnes a year through packaging improvements alone, saving tens of billions of dong. It also collects and recycles milk cartons, the company said at a Hanoi food safety workshop on 28 October.

stories.title: Nahar Poly Films' quarterly revenue rises about 62%
stories.summary: BOPP film maker Nahar Poly Films reported second quarter revenue from operations of ₹258.93 crore, up from ₹159.92 crore a year earlier, a rise of about 61.9 per cent. Total income for the quarter reached ₹262.99 crore against ₹164.55 crore in the same quarter last year.

stories.title: BLS Polymers IPO ends subscribed more than 241 times
stories.summary: BLS Polymers' Rs 255 crore IPO was subscribed a little over 241 times, among the most subscribed primary offers in recent times. Against nearly 1.2 crore shares on offer, bids at the top of the Rs 141 to 150 band came to about 287 crore shares.

stories.title: Energy prices keep pressure on plastics costs
stories.summary: Inflation rose to 3.7 per cent year on year in September, driven mainly by a 20.4 per cent surge in energy prices linked to the geopolitical conflict involving Iran, PlasticsToday reports. The site says energy driven inflation is keeping pressure on costs across the plastics industry.

stories.title: LyondellBasell returns to profit but misses on weak polymer prices
stories.summary: LyondellBasell earned $758 million in the third quarter against a loss of $890 million a year earlier, and revenue rose 10 per cent to $8.5 billion. Adjusted earnings of $2.54 a share still missed the consensus by 7 per cent, as weaker polymer pricing offset strong oxyfuels margins.

stories.title: Opinion: India's waste still travels the wrong way
stories.summary: A Daily Pioneer opinion piece says India talks eloquently about waste to wealth while much of its waste leaves the country as low value scrap or ends up in informal dumps and incinerators, and factories import processed material. Unless recycling systems are fixed, it argues, the promise stays rhetoric.

stories.title: US reinstates Eastman's $375 million recycling grant
stories.summary: The US Department of Energy has reinstated a $375 million grant to Eastman that was cancelled last year, Resource Recycling reports. It will cover expanding the Kingsport methanolysis plant and developing a possible second plant. On an earnings call, CEO Mark Costa hinted at buying recently closed RPET capacity.

stories.title: Study finds recycled flexible film works for non-food uses
stories.summary: A study of curbside collected multilayer flexible film found non-food-contact polyethylene recyclable at commercial scale, PlasticsToday reports, while food contact material still needs further development. The film can come back as something useful, just not yet as something that touches lunch.

stories.title: PlasticsToday calls plastic circularity's barriers real but solvable
stories.summary: PlasticsToday says plastic circularity faces infrastructure, sorting and economic barriers, and argues that new technology, policy mechanisms and cross sector collaboration are driving real progress toward measurable reduction goals. The headline settles on real but solvable, which covers most problems in recycling.

stories.title: Cleanfarms records its biggest year for farm plastics recovery
stories.summary: Canadian producer responsibility organisation Cleanfarms says farmers brought more than 26 million pounds of agricultural plastics to its sites for recycling in 2025, a record for the programme, Recycling Today reports. The figure covers material dropped off at its collection sites.

stories.title: Lotte Chemical backs five waste plastic recycling ventures
stories.summary: Lotte Chemical has picked five waste plastic recycling ventures for the fifth cohort of Project Loop Social, its support programme, and will help them commercialise products. This year it widened eligibility beyond recycled material producers to firms building products and services that use them, Financial News reports.

stories.title: Renegade Plastics gets a loan for recyclable polypropylene for textiles
stories.summary: Renegade Plastics has received a loan to support a production line making recyclable polypropylene for textiles, Recycling Today reports. The funding came from Closed Loop Partners through its Catalytic Capital and Private Credit group. The plastic in question is headed for the wardrobe.

stories.title: Romania's can recycling rate reaches 80.5%
stories.summary: Romania's aluminium can recycling rate rose to 80.5 per cent in the first nine months of 2026 from 75 per cent a year earlier, according to RetuRO, the deposit return system administrator, as analysed by Every Can Counts. Can returns were 6.3 per cent higher than a year before.

stories.title: Every Can Counts collects 80,000 cans at UK events
stories.summary: Every Can Counts collected an estimated 80,000 cans at nine UK music, sports and regional events, including Radio 1's Big Weekend and Download Festival. At Download, 14 ambassadors gathered about 35,000 cans over five days. The Red Bull Soapbox Race added about 6,000 in a single day.

stories.title: Spain tests digital passports for reusable packaging
stories.summary: Spanish plastics technology centre Aimplas is testing digital product passports to trace packaging and validate reuse schemes through its Verso project, with ITC Packaging and waste firm Reciclamas. The research is funded by IVACE+i through the European Regional Development Fund and builds on an earlier project called Oasis.

stories.title: Dutch supermarkets stock a wine bottle that brands share
stories.summary: Non-profit Enviu's Universal Reusable Wine Bottle is now stocked in every Ekoplaza store in the Netherlands, designed so different wine brands can share one bottle. Used bottles are returned, washed, refilled and sold again. Weijnschenk is the first brand to fill it.

stories.title: EPR moves from policy talk into US recycling programmes
stories.summary: Extended producer responsibility is moving from policy discussion into actual recycling programmes, American Recycler reports, as seven US states put producer responsibility schemes into various stages of implementation. Plastics recyclers are watching whether the new funding strengthens collection, processing and end markets.

stories.title: ProPublica examines two US bills on recycling labels
stories.summary: ProPublica reports that two bipartisan US House bills championed by the plastics industry promise national standards for recycling labels, but would give misleading recycling claims the backing of federal law, according to its reporting. The story by Lisa Song was republished by NewsGram.

stories.title: German food groups urge Berlin to drop sugar and plastic taxes
stories.summary: German food and beverage industry groups have urged the federal government to drop planned taxes on sugary drinks and plastic, saying they would raise costs and force new compliance systems. In a joint statement on 29 October, they argued the measures run against Berlin's own pledge to cut red tape.

stories.title: What England and Northern Ireland's deposit return scheme asks of drinks makers
stories.summary: England and Northern Ireland's deposit return scheme launches on 1 October 2027 with a 20p deposit on PET bottles and aluminium and steel cans. Manufacturers must update packaging, labelling and barcodes, BeverageDaily reports, while producer fees are set at zero until the end of 2028.

stories.title: Scotland consults on a household recycling code of conduct
stories.summary: The Scottish Government has opened a consultation on a household recycling code of conduct, which ministers say will make recycling easier and cut carbon emissions, the Scottish Daily Express reports. The paper's coverage focuses on which rubbish items could put households at risk of a fine.

stories.title: WRAP welcomes the UK's inflation linked Plastic Packaging Tax rise
stories.summary: WRAP welcomed the UK Budget's inflation linked rise in Plastic Packaging Tax. Its senior specialist Adam Herriott said HMRC analysis shows UK Plastics Pact members and associates consistently beat non-members on the 30 per cent recycled content threshold. The BPF and FDF also responded, Packaging News reports.

stories.title: Packaging and processing firms give their verdict on the UK Budget
stories.summary: Sustainable Packaging News gathered snap reactions from packaging and processing industry figures to Chancellor John Healey's 2026 Budget, amid material costs, energy prices, supply chain disruption and changing regulation. Media briefings had promised a boring Budget, and the piece checks whether it was.

stories.title: Four Indian ventures find new uses for sugarcane waste
stories.summary: The Better India profiles Indian ventures finding uses for bagasse, the fibre left after sugarcane is crushed, from compostable plates and takeaway boxes to fermentation based protein. They include Chuk, which grew out of Ved Krishna's family paper business in Ayodhya and makes compostable tableware.

stories.title: A Mumbai startup makes spoons you can eat
stories.summary: Mumbai startup Edybites, founded in 2022 by Rupesh K Sanghvi, makes spoons from a millet and flour based mix that are meant to be eaten at the end of a meal, and to decompose naturally if left. At one Ganpati gathering, the children bit in first while the adults watched.

stories.title: South Korean study finds paper straws may be worse than plastic
stories.summary: A study commissioned by South Korea's climate and environment ministry compared plastic, paper, biodegradable plastic and bio-PE straws across 16 environmental categories, from raw materials to disposal. Conventional plastic straws had the lowest impact in 10 of them, including climate change and human toxicity.

stories.title: EcoSource, REEL and Transcend make a paper ice bucket
stories.summary: EcoSource, REEL and Transcend have made REELchilla, a paper ice bucket said to be PE-free, PLA-free, PFAS-free and fossil-free. It ships flat, assembles in seconds and holds a 750ml bottle or four 330ml cans with ice, staying leak resistant for hours.

stories.title: Z1RO makes moulded fibre packaging from non-wood biomass
stories.summary: Z1RO, a finalist in the Start-Up New Materials category of Packaging Europe's 2026 Sustainability Awards, develops biodesigned moulded fibre packaging from non-wood biomass. Founder Alexander Sobolenko explained the project and its next steps in an interview with Packaging Europe.

stories.title: Tea envelopes move toward fibre based packaging
stories.summary: A Tea and Coffee Trade Journal feature by Kerstin Dietze looks at tea brands moving to fibre based envelopes, and how barrier papers can protect product and aroma while staying recyclable with paper waste. It also covers running paper on high speed tea lines. The full article is for subscribers.

stories.title: CBE JU pushes bio-based packaging toward scale-up
stories.summary: The Circular Bio-based Europe Joint Undertaking showcased 29 bio-based solutions at the Global Bioeconomy Summit in Dublin and said bio-based packaging must move from research to industrial scale-up and investment. A workshop it co-hosted called for primary producers to be more involved in bio-based value chains.

stories.title: International Paper counts a $55 million hit from costs
stories.summary: International Paper said inflated costs for energy, fuel and recovered fibre had a $55 million impact, Packaging Dive reports. An investor day next week will focus on separating its European business, as the company prepares to split off the former DS Smith side.

stories.title: Smurfit Westrock's third quarter profit narrows
stories.summary: Smurfit Westrock's third quarter profits narrowed, Recycling Today reports. The containerboard and packaging producer says its North American business enjoyed a higher profit margin than it achieved in other parts of the world, which is where the rest of the business is.

stories.title: Hinojosa keeps its EcoVadis Gold and lifts its score to 84
stories.summary: Hinojosa Packaging Group has kept its EcoVadis Gold medal and raised its score to 84 out of 100 from 80 last year, which the company says puts it among the top 3 per cent of companies assessed globally. The rating covers environmental, social and governance performance.

stories.title: Wyda borrows from baseball cards to package aluminium trays
stories.summary: Brazilian aluminium tray maker Wyda took inspiration from baseball card packaging when developing a product for the US market, where it is eyeing further expansion in the coming years, Packaging Dive reports. Collectors have long known how to sell something flat in a pack.

stories.title: Kocktail swaps cans for reusable glass tumblers
stories.summary: UK small batch maker Kocktail has swapped disposable cans for reusable fluted rocks tumblers, Dieline reports. Each 100ml single serve cocktail at 20 per cent Vol ships in a heavy glass sealed with a brushed brass cap and side pull ring, built to stay in the cupboard afterwards.

stories.title: A camera project swaps plastic for mycelium
stories.summary: Brooklyn mushroom farmer Sree Krishna Pillarisetti's Soft-pixel is a digital camera project with a proposed compostable shell of mycelium, hemp and PHA bioplastic, Yanko Design reports. It is pitched as a successor to the plastic disposable camera, with photos kept local rather than in the cloud.

stories.title: Kongsberg and Parksons Packaging mark 25 years of digital cutting
stories.summary: Kongsberg Precision Cutting Systems and Parksons Packaging are marking 25 years together. Parksons was the first in the region to buy a Kongsberg digital cutting table, in 2001, Emballage Digest reports, helping show the wider Indian packaging industry what digital cutting could do.

stories.title: Nutech Security Printers adds a Rhyguan label inspection machine
stories.summary: Faridabad based Nutech Security Printers, part of Nutech Group, has added a Rhyguan Smart-370 label inspection and converting machine with a Luster camera, supplied and installed by Flexo Image Graphics. The company makes security forms and labels and says it upgrades its machinery regularly.

stories.title: Automation moves into vacuum metallizing
stories.summary: A Sustainable Packaging News feature says automation is becoming necessary in vacuum metallizing as converters and film producers face heat sensitive sustainable substrates, tighter regulations, tougher barrier requirements and a shrinking pool of experienced operators. Machines, it concludes, must get smarter.

stories.title: Truvant picks QAD to standardise seven packaging sites
stories.summary: Truvant, which runs more than 330 production lines across seven packaging and co-manufacturing campuses in North America and Europe, has chosen QAD Redzone to standardise operations on one cloud platform, ERP Today reports. Its sites handle food, household products, vitamins and over the counter medicines.

stories.title: Toyochem gets HACCP certification for packaging coatings
stories.summary: Toyochem Specialty Chemical, part of Japan's artience Group, has received HACCP and Codex Alimentarius certification for its food packaging manufacturing processes, covering its water based coatings. TÜV NORD CERT also renewed its Good Manufacturing Practice certification in August 2026.

stories.title: Battenfeld-Cincinnati begins modernising its Vienna site
stories.summary: Battenfeld-Cincinnati has begun a major modernisation of its Vienna facility, investing millions of euros to upgrade production, processes and working conditions, PlasticsToday reports. The number stays at millions for now, which narrows it down slightly.

stories.title: Plastics and rubber robot orders jump 67.7%
stories.summary: Plastics and rubber robot orders jumped 67.7 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, PlasticsToday reports, as North American automation demand broadened across automotive, electronics and life sciences. The robots, at least, are being hired at pace.

stories.title: Varun Beverages' profit rises 14% as packaging costs weigh
stories.summary: Varun Beverages, PepsiCo's biggest bottler in India, posted a 13.8 per cent rise in third quarter profit to ₹828 crore as volumes grew in India and abroad. Revenue rose 33.3 per cent to ₹6,816 crore, but higher packaging costs pushed total expenses up even faster.

stories.title: Kaira Can's profit jumps 276% with help from a tax adjustment
stories.summary: Kaira Can's net profit rose 276.6 per cent year on year to ₹149.45 lakh in the September quarter, helped by an ₹88.15 lakh tax adjustment from an earlier year. Revenue grew 16.5 per cent to ₹6,493.73 lakh, nearly all of it from tin containers.

stories.title: Pune India Post ships 1,475 Diwali faral parcels abroad
stories.summary: Pune India Post sent 1,475 parcels weighing 10,000 kg overseas between 14 and 27 October under its Diwali Faral Campaign 2026, helping people send traditional sweets and festive snacks to relatives and friends abroad through affordable postal services, Punekar News reports.

stories.title: Aplomb perfume's packaging borrows from wax seals and stamps
stories.summary: Studio Lotta Nieminen built the identity for Scandinavian perfume brand Aplomb, where each fragrance is inspired by a person, around the visual codes of personal correspondence such as wax seals and postal stamps, It's Nice That reports. The aim is the intimacy of a handwritten letter, in a box.

stories.title: Beauty brands are already planning Christmas 2028 advent calendars
stories.summary: BeautyMatter reports that beauty product teams are already discussing Christmas 2028, measuring miniature moisturisers and debating whether a cardboard drawer needs a ribbon, a magnet or new engineering. It is only October 2026. The calendars can cost hundreds and double as a customer acquisition tool.

stories.title: Mondelez says volume led growth is back
stories.summary: Mondelez told analysts that volume led growth is back and here to stay, reporting positive volume and mix in its third quarter and guiding to strong 2027 earnings per share despite inflation. The snack maker also announced it is acquiring Undercover Snacks.

stories.title: Amcor wins two Tube of the Year awards
stories.summary: Amcor won two 2026 Tube of the Year Awards from the Tube Council of North America, in the Pharmaceutical and Personal Care categories, for tubes made with Ocean Potion and Every Man Jack. The awards recognise tube design, decoration, innovation and manufacturing.

stories.title: Snopes looks at the lab grown chocolate rumour
stories.summary: Snopes examined an October rumour that popular chocolate brands have switched to lab grown chocolate and left it unrated, finding it traced to unreliable outlets citing no sources, such as investment firms tipping lab grown cocoa and holistic food blogs. The wrappers, presumably, have not changed.

stories.title: Arthritis Foundation and Tilt Beauty open an Ease of Use Lab
stories.summary: The Arthritis Foundation and Tilt Beauty are opening an Ease of Use Lab in Atlanta that will provide in house lab and human factors evaluation as part of a products and packaging certification programme, Packaging World reports. Lids that open on the first try remain the dream.

stories.title: PepsiCo engineer Hayden Bivens on AI and connected packing lines
stories.summary: Packaging World profiles Hayden Bivens, a technical packaging engineer at PepsiCo who led a large project at the company. He talks about how AI and connected manufacturing will shape the industry, and describes a weight verification system as the handshake between two scales.

stories.title: Peak Milk updates its packs with the new SON logo
stories.summary: Nigerian dairy brand Peak Milk is updating its packaging to carry the new Standards Organisation of Nigeria logo across its range. Packs with the old logo will be phased out gradually, and the company says the products inside are the same. Quality, it says, is at the heart of everything.

stories.title: Why packaging is the face of beauty and fashion brands
stories.summary: A dscene magazine essay argues packaging is often the most recognisable part of beauty and fashion brands, since a serum bottle is picked up every morning and evening and a fragrance sits on a dressing table for months. It calls packaging the point where a style guide becomes an object.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh plans a ₹775 crore packaging hub
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has highlighted a planned Universal Packaging Hub with an investment of ₹775 crore, projected to create 1,880 direct jobs, among proposed industrial investments, DNP India reports, citing a state government post on X. The projects also cover agricultural processing and waste management.

stories.title: Turkish group Desi Kimya buys a UK protective packaging firm
stories.summary: Turkish group Desi Kimya has bought Middlesex based Technology Packaging, its first UK acquisition, Bdaily reports. Technology Packaging supplies protective packaging, corrosion prevention and moisture control products to metal component makers in the automotive, aerospace and medical sectors through its TechCorro brand.

stories.title: International Paper leads a $36 million round for smart radios
stories.summary: International Paper led a $36 million funding round for Relay, a maker of smart radios for frontline communication, Packaging Dive reports. IP trialled the technology at a site in Tampa, Florida, and already uses it at more than 20 of its locations.

stories.title: ProAmpac's leaders talk 2027 deals and active packaging
stories.summary: ProAmpac's president and chief technology officer discussed the acquisition of TC Transcontinental, active packaging, AI and the company's interest in the meat and cheese market in an interview with Packaging Dive about 2027 M&A and innovation predictions.

stories.title: Millcraft plans a Chattanooga division, details to follow
stories.summary: Ohio based paper and packaging distributor Millcraft plans to open a Chattanooga division and recruit for sales, operations, delivery and customer service. The family owned company has not announced a location, opening date, investment or job numbers. Reed Harman will lead it as regional vice president of sales.

stories.title: Verdis completes a $475 million refinancing
stories.summary: Backers of Denmark based waste and recycling services provider Verdis say they have completed a $475 million refinancing arrangement, Recycling Today reports, closing out the company's recapitalisation programme. Recycling, it seems, applies to debt too.

stories.title: Richards Group's packaging revenue falls 7.3%
stories.summary: Richards Group's third quarter revenue rose 1.8 per cent, driven by its May acquisition of PharmaSystems, while packaging revenue fell 7.3 per cent, a smaller drop than the 14.4 per cent in the first half. Gross margins grew 6.5 per cent on a stronger healthcare mix.

events.name: Navigating the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation
events.line: Enterprise Ireland webinar with Repak on PPWR producer duties, reporting and Ireland's EPR transition.

events.name: Navigating Design-for-Recycling of Flexible Packaging
events.line: Recyda webinar on EN 18120 standards, PPWR and EPR fee implications for flexible packaging, with a live digital assessment demo.

events.name: Is Your Packaging Portfolio Ready for PPWR Compliance?
events.line: Intertek webinar on PPWR testing, recycled content verification, PFAS and heavy metals for packaging portfolios.

events.name: EU PPWR practical guidance for non-EU operators (AGRINFO)
events.line: AGRINFO webinar on PPWR declarations of conformity and technical docs for agri-food exporters outside the EU. Second sitting later the same day.

events.name: World Circular Plastics and Waste-to-Value Summit 2026
events.line: Recyclers, brand owners and polymer makers on recycled-content strategy, sorting and packaging rules.

research.title: Hidden Phase Transition in Single-Polymer Stretching under Elongational Flow
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Using machine learning, we identify a second transition in polymer chain stretching driven by planar elongational flow, beyond the well-known coil-stretch transition. We achieve this by developing a conditional extension of Universal and Identifiable Dissipative Dynamics. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: PolyDiscover: an integrated trust-aware platform for multi-objective polymer discovery and simulation validation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Data-driven polymer discovery remains fragmented across databases, models, screening, literature, and simulations. We present PolyDiscover, a platform unifying multi-source property lookup, graph-neural-network prediction, trust-aware multi-objective screening, literature extraction, generative candidate exploration, and automated handoff to molecular-dynamics. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Resisting Drying Stress in Laponite Bentonite Clay Composites, Two Step Yielding and Crack Peel Selection
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Clay films that dry on a rigid substrate crack, peel or stay intact, and which of these happens matters for coatings, barrier layers and ceramic processing. Composites of clay with polymers have been studied widely. Clay. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Response of Hydrogels and Microgels to Nanoparticle Crowding
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Internal degrees of freedom of cross-linked polymer networks enable compressible hydrogels and microgels to swell or deswell by absorbing or expelling solvent in response to environmental changes. Macromolecules in solution can influence the swelling response by. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
